You will need:

  • A printout of the World Cup sheet (or use it to draw your own)
  • Something to write with
  • Sixteen scraps of paper

How to play:

  1. For each pair of books, each player must choose a book to support.
  2. Think of reasons why your book is better than the other.
  3. Debate which book should go through to the next round, sharing your reasons. You need to argue for your book, but eventually you will need to come to an agreement.
  4. Write the winning book in the ‘Quarter Finals’ space.
  5. Repeat with the other books in the ‘Last Sixteen’ round so you end up with eight quarter-finalists.
  6. Once you have all your quarter-finalists, repeat the process with your new pairs to see which four books go through to the Semi Finals.
  7. Repeat your debate with your semi-finalists to fund your two finalists.
  8. Debate your two finalists to find out who wins the award ‘Best Children’s Book of All Time’!

Setting up:

  1. Choose sixteen children’s books that could potentially win the competition ‘Best Children’s Book of All Time’. Remember, it can include any children’s books you like, including picture books and novels. It is fun to have a mix! Make sure you both know all the books!
  2. Write the book titles on separate scraps of paper. Put them into a bowl or hat.
  3. Pull out two titles at a time and write the pairs onto the World Cup sheet in the ‘Last Sixteen’ spaces.
  4. Keep going until all the ‘Last Sixteen’ spaces are filled.
